title: Great House Farm, Llandough (Sir Herbert of Swansea to Vaughan)
authority: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
wdtk_status: Awaiting classification (WhatDoTheyKnow label, as at 24 November 2026)
outcome: Two Department replies: on 20 November (FOI2026/36329) and 23 November 2026 (FOI2026/36556) it said it could not treat the request as one for recorded information. These are the Department's own decisions, not a records search result. WhatDoTheyKnow classification is still pending, so the page does not apply a WhatDoTheyKnow status. Internal review is offered by the Department within 40 working days of each reply; none has been requested on this thread.

deadlines.label: Response (20 working days)
deadlines.result: not assessed: the Department said it could not treat the request as a valid request, so whether and when a clock started is disputed

messages.summary: FOI and policy enquiry to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government on BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 and the Commonhold and Leasehold Reform Bill (clauses 176 to 180): asks for recorded information and, separately, a policy response from the officials responsible for the Bill.

Supplementary clarification attached to the original request: the requester is not asserting that BP lacked registered title, and sets out a narrower question on the legal effect of registration, possession and succession.

Reply FOI2026/36329 (letter attached): the Department says it is unable to treat the request as a valid request for recorded information on this occasion, points to Information Commissioner guidance on writing requests, and offers an internal review (not a statutory process) within 40 working days.
messages.response_class: not treated as a valid request

messages.summary: Restructured request in reply to FOI2026/36329: Part A asks only for recorded information already held; Part B is a separate policy request.

Reply FOI2026/36556 (letter attached): the Department says it is unable to proceed because most of the request appears to ask for legal advice, directs Part B to its correspondence portal, invites a clearer resubmission defining the recorded information sought, and offers an internal review within 40 working days.
